title: 8. Strata: a defined set of layers

sections.name: words
sections.label: The question
sections.content: The owner, 2026-11-27: "Does an srs document need to define a set of layers? I want a human to be able to view the minutes and then drill down. But the current experiences of drilling down feel difficult. Once we drill we have a graph or a mess. What if we actually created a defined set of strata?"

sections.name: answer
sections.label: Answer
sections.content: Yes. A document type should declare its strata: an ordered list of layers, each naming the record types in it. Drill down then means one stratum down, following only relations that mean rests on, and everything else a record relates to falls into a few named directions. The lab's earlier strata experiment made the same choice for writing (a declared mapping, not an inference) and left a trigger to revisit if a package should declare its own layer.

sections.name: measured
sections.label: What was measured
sections.content: Five strata declared for minutes: memory, record, working, evidence, source. In a master holding two real meetings, 600 of 850 relations mean rests on and 250 are arrangement. Within a meeting all 483 rests-on relations go down or stay level: 209 one stratum down, 180 skipping one, 110 within a stratum. The only upward ones cross meetings, which is back in time, not up; 89 more go to standing records beside the meeting. On the LiveWyer Insight report, with strata opportunity, problem, finding, talk, event, all 737 rests-on relations go exactly one stratum down.

sections.name: directions
sections.label: Four directions, not a graph
sections.content: Down: what this rests on, stratum by stratum, to the source. Back and forward: the same matter at other documents of the series. Across: standing records beside the document. Around: its topic and subject. A page built on this shows a meeting's minutes as fixed bands; picking a minute fills each band beneath with only what it rests on at that depth, with the subject and its standing above and standing records and other meetings beside.

sections.name: unifies
sections.label: What it unifies
sections.content: Drill-down. What merges into a master and what stays in the meeting file (the mark the project definition said needed a ruling is the stratum). The rules for minutes: what the meeting did comes from below, context comes from across or back, and one may not be presented as the other. Search defaults. And a check on the Protocol: a stage writes into one stratum and rests only on strata below.

sections.name: levels
sections.label: Where it goes
sections.content: Spec: a strata list on the Blueprint and one invariant, no upward provenance inside a document. A relation type's category (evidence, derivation, provenance) already says which relations mean rests on; which end rests on which is only prose today. Engine: a drill query; merge or slice by stratum; the check. Package: the declaration, and its own relations filed under the right category. Processor and editor: the page.
